1.title: Understanding Teen Depression
1.goal: Help parents recognize signs of depression, understand the teen brain, and differentiate depression from typical teen behavior.
keyConcepts: The adolescent brain is still developing—especially areas related to emotion regulation and impulse control.
Depression in teens can appear as irritability, withdrawal, or academic decline—not just sadness.
Anxiety and depression are often linked in teens.

books.title: The Teenage Brain
books.author: Frances E. Jensen
books.summary: Neuroscience of adolescence; hormonal & brain-based factors behind behavior.

books.title: Helping Your Anxious Teen
books.author: Sheila Achar Josephs
books.summary: How anxiety fuels depressive symptoms and how parents can respond helpfully.

1.title: Building Connection and Emotional Safety
1.goal: Strengthen parent-child communication and establish a home environment where teens feel safe to express themselves.
keyConcepts: Teens need connection, not correction, when they're struggling.
Parents should aim to listen to understand, not just respond.

books.title: Parenting a Teen Who Has Intense Emotions
books.author: Pat Harvey & Jeanine A. Penzo
books.summary: Use DBT-based strategies to reduce emotional outbursts and conflict.

books.title: How to Talk So Teens Will Listen & Listen So Teens Will Talk
books.author: Adele Faber & Elaine Mazlish
books.summary: Teaches reflective listening, respectful boundaries, and problem-solving.

1.title: Equipping Parents with Therapeutic Tools
1.goal: Introduce parents to therapeutic methods (DBT, CBT, mindfulness) they can use to support their teen's emotional regulation.
keyConcepts: DBT emphasizes validation and skill-building (e.g., distress tolerance, emotion regulation).
CBT focuses on reframing negative thought patterns.
Parents can model and reinforce these techniques at home.

books.title: The Whole-Brain Child
books.author: Daniel J. Siegel & Tina Payne Bryson
books.summary: 12 practical strategies to integrate emotional and rational brain development.

books.title: The DBT Skills Workbook for Parents of Teens
books.author: Joss Reed
books.summary: Teaches DBT tools like “Wise Mind” and “DEAR MAN” for effective parenting.

1.title: Supporting Recovery and Resilience
1.goal: Help teens develop skills to recover from depressive episodes and grow emotional resilience.
keyConcepts: Mindfulness enhances emotional awareness and reduces reactivity.
Recovery isn’t linear—setbacks are part of the process.
Parental support is a critical protective factor.

books.title: The Mindful Teen
books.author: Dzung X. Vo
books.summary: Mindfulness tools for teens that parents can model and support.

books.title: Cognitive Behavioral Therapy for Teens
books.author: Michelle G. Craske
books.summary: Workbook-style CBT strategies that help teens challenge unhelpful thoughts.

1.title: Long-Term Growth and Prevention
1.goal: Promote long-term mental wellness and prepare for life beyond the depressive episode.
keyConcepts: Mood disorders require long-term strategies, not just crisis interventions.
Adolescence is a time of transformation—supporting strengths is just as critical as managing symptoms.
Parents can become growth partners, not just caretakers.

books.title: Raising a Moody Child
books.author: Mary A. Fristad & Jill S. Goldberg Arnold
books.summary: Build routines, reinforce strengths, and prepare for relapse prevention.

books.title: Brainstorm
books.author: Daniel J. Siegel
books.summary: Reframes adolescence as a unique, powerful life stage full of opportunity.
